trigger: Partners want a contract review pilot before the next financial year

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: Daniel, thanks for making the time. I have you as Daniel Ortiz, Operations Lead at Kite & Co, a commercial law firm in the CBD. What prompted you to take the call with Eleno?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: That is right. Our partners have asked for a contract review pilot before the next financial year. They have all read the same three articles and now want to know why we are still reading leases line by line.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: What sort of contracts, and what volume are we talking about?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: Mostly commercial leases and supply agreements. The property team alone reviews around ninety leases a quarter, and a first-pass review of a lease is two to four hours for a junior before a partner looks at it at all.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: What does that first pass actually involve?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: Pulling the key dates, the rent review mechanism, assignment and make-good clauses and anything unusual into a summary the partner reads. Ninety per cent of it is the same fields every single time. The judgement is in the other ten per cent.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: Where do the documents sit, and what does the summary get written into?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: Documents are in our practice management system and summaries are Word memos saved against the matter. There is a precedent template that everyone has quietly modified, so no two summaries look the same, which the partners complain about constantly.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: If the pilot works, what does the partner group see that convinces them?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: A junior producing a first-pass summary in twenty minutes instead of three hours, with the same fields every time, and a partner able to see where each field came from in the document. If they cannot trace it back to the clause they will not trust it.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: And who decides whether the pilot becomes a project?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: The partnership decides, which is eleven people who meet monthly. I can recommend it and I can find budget for a pilot inside the operations line, but a build of any real size goes to them.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: Understood. What I would propose is a two-week discovery phase on the property team's lease review, then a fixed-scope build of a clause extraction and summary agent that writes into your precedent template with a link back to the source clause. For ninety leases a quarter plus the supply agreements, that build sits around $132,000.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: That number has to go to the partnership, and they will not approve it before they have seen the pilot work on our own leases.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: That is reasonable, and it is why the discovery phase is priced and scoped separately. It is small enough to sit inside your operations line, and at the end you have a measured baseline and output on your own documents to put in front of them.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: That helps. What I cannot give you is a date for the partnership, because the next meeting agenda is already full and the one after that is the financial year planning session.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: Then let us work to what you control. If the discovery phase runs this month, you walk into the planning session with real output instead of a proposal.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: In principle yes. In practice I need the managing partner to agree to the discovery phase first, and he is in a hearing until the end of next week.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: Is there anything I can put in his hands that makes that a five-minute conversation?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: A single page with the cost, the two weeks and exactly which leases you would work on. He will not read more than a page before he is back in front of a client.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: I will send a one-page discovery phase scope by Friday. I will send a redacted sample summary from a lease you provide as well, so he is looking at output rather than a description of it.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: Send the scope first. I will not have a lease cleared for you to use until our risk partner signs off the confidentiality side, and that takes its own week.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: Understood. We can work from a publicly available lease in the meantime so nobody has to clear anything, then swap to yours once it is approved.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: That would help, although the partners will say a public lease proves nothing about our precedents.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: They would be right, which is why it is a stopgap rather than the evidence. The evidence is the discovery phase on your own files, with your own template.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: Agreed. Realistically I am looking at getting this in front of the partnership in October, not September, and I would rather tell you that now than string it out.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.name: Sam Whitfield
turns.text: I appreciate it. I will keep the scope current and check in the week the hearing finishes. If the managing partner wants to talk before then I can be in the CBD at a day's notice.

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.name: Daniel Ortiz
turns.text: That works. I will come back to you once I know whether the discovery phase can come out of operations without the partnership signing it off first.
